# TopologyGroups' native history witness pops out a pane too wide to stage

## Context

The full Workstation NL tier at `dev` `3ec6e0b945` (run locally, since hosted CI selects none of it) reds one case: `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` › "a human dock action then a popup move append ordered rows, and undo reverses them newest-first". The failure is "two free native positions must fit the display". The origin popup is 1176×240, the main window is 1200×949 at (22, 109), and the screen is 1920×1080.

## The Problem

The witness pops out the Feed pane, a full-width bottom strip. A header pop-out opens at the pane's real footprint (#19597 / #19598, restoring the operator's contract for the header pop-out). So `freePopupPlacement` can find no corner for it beside main.

The case was red the same way at `5ccdb192d6^`, before #19559, and passed only during #19559's 480×360 fallback. Its subject is the history rows of a native popup move. The popped pane is incidental; its title only selects the pop-out and checks that the popup is present.

## The Architectural Reality

- `freePopupPlacement` tries the four screen corners for a popup of the origin's size, 16 px clear of every live target (#19480, merged in #19481).
- The case's strict contract, which Euclid restated as the author of #19480:
  - the dock row precedes the `native-popup-move` rows;
  - the Group, binding and placement generation stay unchanged;
  - undo runs newest first, and `alerts.locked` survives until its own row is undone;
  - redo runs without history growth.

## The Fix

Pop out a right-column pane (`Commits`, about 355×519) instead of Feed. Keep `freePopupPlacement` and every history and geometry assertion strict. Do not force fallback sizing and do not enlarge the screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The case passes locally at the PR head, with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set, and its assertions are unchanged apart from the pane selection.
- [ ] The rest of `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` stays green.

## Out of Scope

- Running this tier in hosted CI (D#19599).
